evidence-grounded.why: The criterion holds: the output has two FAIL lines and no PASS lines, and each FAIL names a concrete wrong build. Line 1: wrapping JSON.parse in try/catch and returning {} meets the line. But app.js then merges {} into DEFAULTS and prints "listening on 8080" with no error, so the typo is hidden. That misses the request's "can't tell which file is broken or where." Line 2: deleting the "bad JSON throws" test lets npm test pass with nothing checking that the file path or error position is reported. I checked every citation against the repository and all are real: test/config.test.js:15 is the SyntaxError test, the README promises "bad config: <message>" and exit 1, app.js's DEFAULTS sets port 8080, and the spread merge behaves as described.

catches-traps.why: The must_catch list has one item: line 1 has to FAIL because the app would start on defaults and nobody would learn which file is broken or where the mistake is. I checked the output's verdict for line 1. It is "FAIL". The evidence says that if loadConfig returns {}, app.js "prints 'listening on 8080' with no message at all, so the typo is hidden completely". It ties this back to the request: people "can't tell which file is broken or where the mistake is". It also says a correct fix should report the file path and the line/column of the error. The wrong_build section makes the same point: the app "silently starts on the default port 8080 with no error". Every part of the trap is covered, so the criterion holds.

avoids-must-not.why: The must_not list has one item: a PASS on line 1. Line 1 is "loadConfig(path) in src/config.js returns {} when the file is not valid JSON". The output marks it "result": "FAIL". It explains that returning {} would hide the typo, since app.js would start on port 8080 with no message, and that it would break the README's "bad config: <message>" / exit 1 behavior. Nothing in the output gives line 1 a PASS. The overall result and line 2 are also FAIL. So the output does nothing on the must_not list.
